title: Attended DL4SCI Summer School 2026
description: Spent five days at Berkeley Lab for the DL4SCI (Deep Learning for Science) Summer School, where I presented a poster on DIVER, our foundation model for intracranial and scalp EEG. The most fun part was seeing foundation models applied way outside neuroscience — climate, physics, astronomy — and swapping notes with people wrestling with completely different data and constraints. Watching those design choices diverge by domain actually sharpened my sense of what's genuinely distinctive about building foundation models for the brain, instead of just importing recipes from vision or language. Came away with a clearer read on what matters for brain-FM work and a great group of people to keep comparing notes with.

title: Released LucyPlanner, a macOS day planner
description: Built and open-sourced LucyPlanner, a small macOS app I made because no existing planner kept my daily goal, time table, todos, and habits all on one screen. It's SwiftUI + SwiftData under the hood, integrates with Apple Calendar via EventKit, and includes a lightweight Eisenhower matrix view for triaging what's actually urgent versus what just feels loud. Source, download, and setup notes at github.com/yahyunee/LucyPlanner.

title: Attended ACM CAIS 2026
description: Spent four days in San Jose at ACM CAIS 2026 (AI and agentic systems). Really enjoyed diving into agentic AI across talks, workshops, and demos. One nice surprise was seeing a few sessions on AI scientists — got me thinking about how far we can (and should) let AI reach into science. Also got a real taste of the Silicon Valley vibe, and loved meeting new people from labs and companies I hadn't crossed paths with before.

title: 2026 ALCF INCITE GPU Hackathon
description: Spent three days at Argonne with team DIVER, working with ALCF mentors to scale our code on Aurora, Polaris, and the AI Testbeds in preparation for our INCITE proposal. Gave both the kickoff and final presentations, learned a ton about distributed GPU workflows, and met an incredible group of researchers from across the country.

title: Started VSRC at Princeton University
description: Began my time at Princeton University as a Visiting Student Research Collaborator (VSRC) from April through September 2026. Excited to dive into new research, meet the people here, and make the most of these six months on campus.
